en.title: Michael Credico's Technicolor Horses Reveals Surreal Heartland in New Cover
en.summary: The cover for Michael Credico's upcoming novella, Technicolor Horses, has been unveiled, offering a glimpse into a near-future American Midwest grappling with disaster. Published by Autumn House Press on April 6, 2027, the book explores themes of trust erosion and dwindling hope.
en.body:
The literary world is abuzz with the exclusive cover reveal for **Michael Credico**’s forthcoming novella, **Technicolor Horses**. Set to be released by **Autumn House Press** on April 6, 2027, the artwork, designed by **Kinsley Stocum**, hints at the unsettling and evocative landscape within.

**Technicolor Horses** plunges readers into a near-future American Midwest, specifically an Ohio community reeling from a catastrophic drought. As the ecosystem collapses, so too does the fabric of trust among its inhabitants. Water becomes a precious commodity, loved ones vanish, and societal systems begin to crumble, leaving a populace struggling to make sense of the chaos. Credico's work is described as a potent blend of warning, elegy, and a deeply human plea for what might still be possible in a world teetering on the brink. The narrative navigates a surreal heartland where the lines of authority blur, and the familiar unravels with disquieting speed.

Credico, known for his thematic focus—his first book, **Heartland Calamitous**, was famously "The Fish Book"—explains that **Technicolor Horses** is very much "The Horse Book." His fascination with acid westerns and the speculative visions of filmmakers like Alejandro Jodorowsky clearly informs the novella's unique atmosphere. The story delves into fragmented lives shaped by loss and surveillance, where hope flickers precariously. Despite the encroaching desolation, the titular horses, once vibrant, continue their relentless journey, a powerful metaphor for enduring spirit in the face of overwhelming odds. "I tend to write fixated on certain images and ideas. Sometimes for years at a time. I have phases," Credico has stated, underscoring his dedicated approach to exploring singular concepts.

## A World on the Brink

The novella's exploration of a community under duress resonates deeply with contemporary anxieties. The breakdown of trust, the scarcity of resources, and the erosion of familiar structures are themes that speak directly to a global audience increasingly concerned with environmental collapse and societal instability. **Technicolor Horses** promises a narrative that is both a mirror to our current fears and a poignant reflection on the resilience of the human spirit, even when faced with dwindling hope and surreal circumstances. The imagery of ditchdiggers replaced by interns and protestors in rubber horse masks paints a vivid picture of a society grappling with absurdities born from crisis.

## What to Expect

With its compelling themes and unique stylistic approach, **Technicolor Horses** is poised to be a significant release for fans of speculative fiction and literary novellas. The cover art itself serves as an invitation into a world both strange and familiar, promising a reading experience that is both thought-provoking and emotionally resonant. Readers can anticipate a narrative that, much like its titular steeds, keeps moving forward, even when the landscape around it is fading.

## What's Next

**Technicolor Horses** by **Michael Credico** is scheduled for release on April 6, 2027, by **Autumn House Press**. Pre-orders are currently available, offering eager readers a chance to secure their copy of this anticipated novella.

content_raw: Electric Literature is pleased to reveal the cover of Technicolor Horses by Michael Credico, which will be published on April 6, 2027 by Autumn House Press. You can pre-order your copy here . Set in a near-future version of the American Midwest, Michael Credico’s novella, Technicolor Horses , explores the disaster of an Ohio community caught in chaos and how trust erodes alongside their drought-ridden ecosystem. Water is scarce. Loved ones are missing. Systems are breaking down. And nobody seems able to make sense of it all. Technicolor Horses is part warning, part elegy, and part deeply human yearning for what might still be possible, taking readers through a surrealist heartland where no one is sure who’s still in charge. In a whirlwind of ditchdiggers replaced by interns, protestors wearing rubber horse masks, flooded streets and lost spouses and children, these fragmented stories ask what happens when the familiar unravels—when memory lapses, language fails, and even a flood feels personal. With dry observation and quiet sorrow, Credico builds his narrative on the lives shaped by loss, surveillance, and strange, flickering, dwindling hope in a world with few answers and no real heroes. And though the horses, once vivid, begin to fade, they don’t stop loping. Here’s the cover, designed by Kinsley Stocum: Michael Credico: I tend to write fixated on certain images and ideas. Sometimes for years at a time. I have phases. My first book, Heartland Calamitous , was, essentially, The Fish Book. Technicolor Horses is very much The Horse Book. I was watching a lot of acid and “electric” westerns. I kept imagining what if Alejandro Jodorowsky had attempted to adapt Wise Blood instead of Dune . I mentioned my interest in these things when we began to think about the cover direction. Kinsley provided this series of strange archival renderings of horses, including the drawing of horses in various states of horseness that ended up being used. I love how bright and outrageous things turned out. I encounter hundreds of books of fiction and poetry each day. I’m a library worker whose main responsibility is getting books from here to there and back again. Doing a job like this for so many years, you really appreciate when a cover breaks up the monotony a bit. I think this one does that. More than anything, I’m grateful to Kinsley for creating something that I think will meaningfully and truthfully inform how readers experience my weird little book. Kinsley Stocum: I like to begin my process by requesting and reviewing inspiration provided by the author, whatever they want to provide: images, colors, other book covers, etc. In this case, Michael was very helpful in narrowing my focus. The inspo he provided was minimalist, rich and colorful, with an emphasis on Spanish-language book covers and movie posters, specifically providing a painting by Leonora Carrington and the poster for the 1932 movie Wild Horse Mesa .
